Definition: to slake the thirst (occasionally of other appetites)
BiblicalUsage: Ravah is to slake the thirst, to water abundantly — occasionally, of other appetites. The psalm says God visits the earth and waters it, 'Thou waterest the ridges thereof abundantly: thou settlest the furrows thereof'; Isaiah says the rain and snow 'water the earth, and make it bring forth and bud'; and God says, 'I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people shall be satisfied with my goodness.'
TheologicalSignificance: The point for me is that God waters the way He waters the earth: abundantly, until the furrows settle and the soul is satisfied with His goodness.
